extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, researchers interested in conspiracy theories and anti-trans rhetoric
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and evaluate the phenomenon of 'transvestigation' — a conspiracy theory alleging celebrities (and others) are secretly transgender — including its methods, harms, social-media spread, and legal consequences. Useful for readers, journalists, and researchers assessing or reporting on such claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods and evidence reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: “Proponents claim to be able to determine the assigned sex of individuals, primarily through photographic and video evidence. The methods used by 'transvestigators' are subject to pareidolia and confirmation bias.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate any investigative claims by testing whether the evidence is visual-only and subject to cognitive biases (pareidolia, confirmation bias). Photographs and video-based speculation are unreliable for determining assigned sex; require corroborating primary-source evidence rather than inferences from appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical conspiratorial basis and motifs
rubrics_metrics.description: “The basis for transvestigation ranges from the belief that some celebrities' gender identity simply differs from their birth-assigned sex, to the belief that their transgender identity is part of an initiation ritual known as 'elite gender inversion', conducted by Hollywood and music industry elites or secret organizations such as the New World Order and Illuminati.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When identifying transvestigation-style claims, look for hallmark conspiracy motifs: grand narratives (elite rituals), secret cabals (Illuminati/New World Order), and pattern-seeking that links unrelated facts. These motifs indicate conspiracy framing rather than evidentiary argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification as transphobia by advocacy groups
rubrics_metrics.description: “GLAAD ... considers the movement to be an expression of transphobia.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting or commentary that amplifies transvestigation claims should consider the assessment of LGBTQ+ advocacy organizations — such claims often function as expressions of prejudice. Editors and reporters should weigh harm and not present such theories neutrally without context about their transphobic character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal risk and defamation consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples in the article: Brigitte Macron filed lawsuits against allegations that she was born male; two women were found guilty of slander (later overturned) argued to have acted in 'good faith'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accusations about a person's gender history can lead to defamation, slander, or false-light litigation. Journalists and individuals should verify facts before repeating allegations; consider jurisdictional libel laws, potential damages, and defenses like good faith and truth. Legal consequences have occurred in multiple countries and can include criminal complaints for harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sports context: susceptibility and harms
rubrics_metrics.description: “Women's sports forms a popular arena for transvestigation ... buttressed by sporting practices such as sex eligibility tests. During the controversy around women's boxing at the 2024 Olympics ... public figures ... asserted that Imane Khelif was a man ... Khelif filed a criminal complaint ... alleging gender-based cyberharassment.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accusations in sport often exploit anxiety about sex verification and rely on appearance rather than evidence. Such claims can cause direct harm (harassment, retractions by outlets, criminal complaints). Reporting on athletes' sex/gender should prioritize athlete safety, rely on authoritative procedures and official statements, and avoid amplifying unverified personal attacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of physiognomy/face-reading is pseudoscience
rubrics_metrics.description: See-also note: “Physiognomy – Pseudoscience of face reading.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques that read identity from facial features (physiognomy) are pseudoscientific and unreliable. Treat any face-reading arguments as lacking scientific credibility and avoid citing them as evidence for claims about a person’s sex or gender.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social-media amplification is not validation
rubrics_metrics.description: “The theories have gained considerable popularity on the social media platform Twitter, especially after Elon Musk's participation in the harassment of Imane Khelif and of his own transgender daughter.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Popularity or amplification on social platforms does not validate factual claims. Assess whether viral spread is driven by harassment, high-profile amplification, or platform dynamics rather than corroborated evidence. Consider platform moderation, public figures' role, and the potential for harm when deciding whether to report or engage with trending allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalistic/ethical anti-patterns to avoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Article categories and related topics include 'pink-slime journalism', 'character assassination', 'tabloid journalism', and 'body shaming'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid practices such as publishing unverified rumors, framing smear pieces as legitimate inquiry, or using sensationalist language that amounts to character assassination. Good journalistic practice requires verification, context about harm and bias, and refusal to amplify material that primarily shames or marginalizes people without substantive evidence.
